about: The plugin names its own agents, skills and mod commands: every `ah:<name>` the Node recordings carry is `<plugin>:<name>` here, where <plugin> is the name the build embedded (ah2). The recordings are not rewritten; the replay reads them with the namespace mapped, so a case's input and its expectation both carry the native name.

rows.recorded: agent types, dispatch names and --agent values `ah:architect`, `ah:implementor`, `ah:reviewer`, `ah:ultra-advisor`, `ah:task-runner`, `ah:orchestrator`, `ah:secret-scanner`
rows.native: `<plugin>:<role>` through IConfigCore.Qualified / BuiltinRoleOf and IAhEnvironment.PluginName(); a build that embedded no name uses wrangl
rows.reason: a second plugin named `ah` would collide with the v1 plugin's agents in Claude Code; gates, the route gate and usage attribution match the plugin's own namespace and ignore `ah:<role>`
skills and commands are namespaced by the plugin that ships them
doctor finds this plugin's install record by its own name

rows.recorded: mod command `hierarchy-pane`, mod state and mount keys `plugin: 'ah'`
rows.reason: the v1 mod's commands carry no plugin prefix, so the v2 mod's are prefixed; its state is keyed by its own name

rows.recorded: case files and fixture trees under tests/contracts spelled with `ah:`
rows.native: read through tests/contract-tools/lib-case.mjs toPluginNamespace (lanes) and Ah.TestKit RecordedNamespace (unit tables and goldens), which rewrite `ah:` followed by a letter, `*`, `<`, `{` or a closing quote when it is not part of a longer word
rows.reason: the Node recordings stay the oracle for every other byte of the output
